reason: The cited evidence shows that ML potentials can be trained for a refractory high-entropy alloy (E1) and that vibrational entropy can be extracted from AIMD configurations (E2), but neither passage demonstrates that an ML potential trained on short AIMD can accurately capture anharmonicity and electron–vibration coupling, nor that it can be coupled with Monte Carlo/free-energy integration to compute phase free energies for both solid and liquid, nor that it achieves the claimed speedup and accuracy for fusion properties. The key premises thus lack direct support.
premises: ML potentials trained on short AIMD can capture anharmonicity and electron–vibration coupling
ML potentials can be used with Monte Carlo or free-energy integration to compute phase free energies
The approach works for multicomponent high-entropy alloys
The method reduces computational cost by an order of magnitude vs. TOR-TILD and explicit AIMD
The method yields fusion properties within ~5% of full AIMD results
